extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders commenting on FERC rulemakings and project reviews (e.g., landowners, affected parties, organizations, attorneys, NGOs, industry)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing effective public comments to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for rulemakings and energy project reviews. Covers how to submit (eComment vs eFiling), procedural steps, and substantive content that strengthens the Commission record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eComment for brief text-only comments
rubrics_metrics.description: For brief, text-only comments – up to 10,000 characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No account required; quickest way to file online. Key/paste text comments in the large text box; a counter shows characters remaining. Best for short submissions that do not require attachments or formal filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eFiling for longer comments or organizational filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For longer comments, attachments, or filings on behalf of an organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires an eRegister account. Use eFiling when you need to submit supporting documents, multiple-file exhibits, or when submitting on behalf of an organization that needs a formal filing record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the eComment submission steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive email with detailed instructions; click link in email to display 'Submit eComment' screen; query and select the docket or project number(s); key or paste text comments in the large text box; counter shows characters remaining
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the step-by-step flow provided in the FERC email/link to ensure the comment is correctly associated with the docket/project. Selecting the correct docket/project number is essential for the comment to be included in the proper record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference the specific docket or project number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the docket or project number ensures FERC can associate your comment with the correct proceeding. This is a basic but essential technical requirement for effective submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the technical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the technical analysis (e.g., transmission planning, rate design)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the substantive technical issues in the filing rather than only expressing general opinions. Concrete engagement with analyses such as transmission planning or rate design helps FERC evaluate factual and technical impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include relevant data (markets, reliability, environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include data on energy markets, reliability impacts, environmental effects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide facts, quantitative data, or studies that support your points. Data-driven comments are more useful to the Commission than purely rhetorical statements. Cite sources and attach supporting documents when appropriate (use eFiling for attachments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite controlling statutes and legal provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Federal Power Act, Natural Gas Act provisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference statutory provisions that are relevant to the issue being commented on to connect arguments to legal standards the Commission applies. Pointing to specific sections of the FPA or NGA helps frame claims within the Commission's legal framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Commission precedent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how prior FERC decisions bear on the current matter. Explaining whether and why precedent supports or undermines a requested outcome helps the Commission evaluate potential departures or consistency with past practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest specific tariff or regulatory text changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest specific tariff or regulatory text changes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete proposed language when asking for regulatory or tariff modifications. Specific edits are more actionable for the Commission than vague recommendations and can be directly evaluated and incorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify yourself as a landowner/affected party when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify yourself as a landowner/affected party where applicable (for pipeline and transmission line reviews)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly stating your status (e.g., landowner, resident, local official) helps FERC assess standing, the nature of impacts, and the weight to give particular concerns. For project reviews, this identification connects comments to on-the-ground effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite NEPA-relevant impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting on energy projects subject to NEPA, focus on environmental impacts that NEPA requires the Commission to consider. Describe potential direct, indirect, and cumulative environmental effects and provide supporting data or references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address environmental justice considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and explain disproportionately high and adverse human health or environmental effects on minority and low-income populations, and provide supporting evidence. Linking EJ concerns to project decisions and mitigation measures is important for the Commission's review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference cumulative impacts of related projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference cumulative impacts of related projects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the project interacts with other past, present, and reasonably foreseeable future projects to create cumulative environmental or reliability impacts. Providing context and evidence about related developments strengthens NEPA and impact analyses.
